abstract.p: Self-disclosure can provide psychological comfort and social support, but it also carries the risk of unintentionally revealing sensitive information, leading to serious privacy concerns. Research on self-disclosure in Chinese multimodal contexts remains limited, lacking highquality corpora, analysis, and methods for detection. This work focuses on self-disclosure behaviors on Chinese multimodal social media platforms and constructs a high-quality textimage corpus to address this critical data gap. We systematically analyze the distribution of self-disclosure types, modality preferences, and their relationship with user intent, uncovering expressive patterns unique to the Chinese multimodal context. We also fine-tune five multimodal large language models to enhance selfdisclosure detection in multimodal scenarios. Among these models, the Qwen2.5-omni-7B achieved a strong performance, with a partial span F1 score of 88.2%. This study provides a novel research perspective on multimodal selfdisclosure in the Chinese context.
